MEMBRAN PLASMA
Membran plasma = membran sel
• Adalah suatu membran yang memisahkan sel dari lingkungan sekelilingnya dan memiliki sifat
selektif permeabel
• Membran sel bersifat fleksibel sehingga organisme uniseluler dapat bergerak
• Homeostasis (equilibrium) pada sel dipertahankan oleh fungsi membran sel yaitu mengatur
bahan yang masuk dan keluar sel

Fungsi membran sel
• Pemisah sel dengan lingkungan luar (protective barrier)
• Regulasi transpor bahan keluar dan masuk sel (selectively permeable)
• Pengenalan sel
• Tempat menambatnya filamen sitoskeleton
• Tempat ikatan enzim
• Tempat perlekatan antar sel (junctions)
• Berisi sitoplasma (cairan di dalam sel)
• Tempat menerima rangsangan dari luar agar sel mampu memberi respon

lemak yang bersifat nonpolar dan

• Membran sel terbentuk dari 2 lapis

• Kepala polar bersifat hidrofilik “suka air”
• Ekor nonpolar bersifat hidrofobik “benci air”
• Menyebabkan membran sel bersifat selektif
terhadap bahan yang melintasi sel
• Fosfolipid bersifat amfipatik: memiliki gugus 
yang bersifat hidrofilik dan hidrofobik

SITOSKELETON
Cytoskeleton 
Cyto +  skeleton = “cell skeleton”
Internal framework of cell
The cell also have skeleton, like 
our body
Microtubules (MTs)
Intermediate Filament (Ifs)
Microfilament/ Actin Filament 
(Actins)
Each of the 3 types of cytoskeletal filament is a polymer of 
protein subunits held together by weak, noncovalent bonds
Structure of Microtubule
Tubular structures, hollow, relatively rigid
Diameter 25 nm, a wall thickness 4 nm, length between 250 nm- 25 μm
Compose of globular proteins arranged in longitudinal rows, termed 
protofilaments
Each protofilament is assembled from dimeric building blocks consisting of 1 α-
tubulin & 1 β-tubulin subunit
In cross section, microtubules are seen to consist of 13 protofilament aligned side 
by side in a circular pattern
One end of a microtubue is known as the plus end and is terminated by row of β-
tubulin subunit. The opposite end is the minus end, and is terminated by a row of 
α-tubulin subunit
Structure of Microtubule
Structure of Microfilament (Actin)
Intermediate Filament (IF)
Unlike microtubules and microfilaments, intermediate filaments are assembled 
from a large number of different IF proteins.
The assembly of intermediate filaments probably proceeds through several 
intermediate structures, which associate by lateral and end-to-end interactions
Intermediate filaments are much more stable than microfilaments and 
microtubules
Major degenerative diseases of skin, muscle, and neurons are caused by disruption 
of the IF cytoskeleton or its connections to other cell structures
IF Structure
• 2 Monomer IF dimer tetramer IF

Cytoskeleton function
Mitotic apparatus (microtubules) 
is designed to attach and capture 
chromosomes, align the 
chromosomes, and then separate 
them so that the genetic material 
is evenly partitioned to each 
daughter cell. Fifteen hours later, 
the whole process is repeated by 
the two daughter cells.
Sentrosom dan Sentriol
• Sentrosom, atau  pusat  sel, terletak  dekat  nukleus,  
tersusun  atas sentriol yang dikelilingi sebuah massa 
protein amorf. 
• Sentrosom  merupakan pusat  pengatur  mikrotubulus  
utama  sel.
• Sentriol adalah sepasang struktur silindris pendek yang 
tegak lurus satu sama lain di bagian  tengah  sentrosom 
• Pada  pembelahan sel,  sentriol  membentuk  gelendong  
mitotik  di  luar mikrotubulus  guna  mengarahkan  
pergerakan  kromosom. 
SISTEM
ENDOMEMBRAN
Endomembranes
• Under the light microscope, the cytoplasm of living cells appears relatively devoid 
of structure
• Before the beginning of the twentieth century, examination of stained sections of 
animal tissues hinted at the existence of an extensive membrane network within 
the cytoplasm
• The development of the electron microscope in the 1940s, that biologist began to 
appreciate the diverse array of membrane-bound structure present in the 
cytoplasm of most eukaryotic cells; long channel bounded by membranes; and 
stacks of flattened membrane-bound sacs (cisternae)
• Cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells was subdivided into a variety of distinct 
compartement bound by membrane barrier and formed different organelles that 
could be identified in diverse cells from yeast to multicellular plants and animal
Endomembrane system
• The endomembrane system is a series 
of compartments that work together 
to package, label, and ship proteins 
and molecules.
• These membrane devide the cell into 
functional and structural compartement
or organella: nuclear membrane, 
endoplasmic reticulum, golgi apparatus, 
lysosomes, endosomes, vesicle and cell 
membrane. 
• These organelles form an 
endomembranes system in which the 
individual components function as part 
of a coordinated unit
Endomembrane System and the Pathway
• Protein, lipid, and complex polysaccharides 
are transported through the cell along the 
biosynthetic or secretory pathway; these 
enclosed by the endomembranes
• The endocytic pathway, materials move from 
the outer surface of the cell to compartement

Vesicle Transport
• Transport vesicles move through the cytoplasm in a 
directed manner, often pulled out by motor protein that 
operated on tracks formed by microtubules and 
microfilament
• When they reach their destination, the vesicles fuse with 
the membrane of the acceptor compartement
• Repeated cycles of budding and fusion shuttle a diverse 
array of materials along numerous pathway that diverse 
the cell
Vesicle Transport
• These vesicle are covered on their cytosolic surface 
by protein coat formed from soluble protein that 
assemble on the cytosolic surface of the donor 
membrane 
• Each coated bud pinches off to form a coated vesicle 
• All types of coated vesicles are formed by 
polymerization of cytosolic coat proteins onto a 
donor (parent) membrane to form vesicle buds that 
eventually pinch off from the membrane to release a 
complete vesicle. 
• Shortly after vesicle release, the coat is shed exposing 
proteins required for fusion with the target 
membrane
Protein coat
Protein coat have 2 distinct function:
1.
As a mechanical device that causes the 
membrane to curve & form budding 
vesicle
2.
Selecting the component to be carried

The Endocytic Pathway
Moving membrane and materials into the cell interior 
involve 2 basic processes : endocytosis and phagocytosis
1.
Endocytosis is primarily a process by which the cell 
internalizes materials from extracelluler :
• Pinocytosis is the nonspecific uptake of extracellular 
fluids; removes portions of the plasma membrane 
(recycling of membrane)
• Receptor-mediated endocytosis (RME) is uptake of  
specific extracellular macromolecules (ligands) following 
their binding to receptors on the external surface of the 
plasma membrane
2.
Phagocytosis or “cell eating” is uptake of relatively 
large particles (>0.5µm) from the environment

• RME provides selective and efficient uptake of

• Cells have receptors for the uptake of many different

• Ligand bind to receptors that collect in specialized

• Coated pits invaginate into the cytoplasm and then

TIGHT JUNCTION 
(zonula occludens)
• Belts of proteins that close extracellular space 
between cells
• Prevent passage of water & water-soluble substances
• Isolate parts of plasma membrane (apical & 
basolateral)
• Look like honey comb
Molecular structure of tight junctions
• Claudins (membrane proteins) zip two 
membranes together
• Stabilized by spectrin
• Connected to spectrin by adapter 
proteins ZO1 and ZO2
Adherens Junction
• Belt-like junctions located just below 
tight junction
• Simple points of attachment, do not 
contain channels connecting the 
interiors of the two attached cells
• Maintains the physical integrity of the 
epithelium
• Confer mechanical strength
Adherens Junction
• Homophilic pairing of E-cadherins
• Adapter proteins (plakoglobin and 
α and βcatenins) link cadherins to 
the belt of actin filaments
DESMOSOM (macula adherens)
• Localized spot-like adhesions randomly 
arranged on sides of plasma membranes. 
• Hold cells tightly together
• Confer mechanical strength
• Common in tissue that are subject to 
severe stress such as skin and cardiac 
muscle
Molecular structure of desmosomes
• Button like welds joining opposing cell 
membranes
• Cadherins bind the membranes of 
adjacent cells in a way that gives strength 
and rigidity to the entire tissue
• Two cadherins: Desmoglein &  
Desmocollin
• Adapter proteins 
• Plakoglobin and desmoplakin
• Linked to epidermal keratins
HEMIDESMOSOMES
• Hemidesmosomes connect an epithelial 
cell to the basal lamina (cell-matrix 
adhesion)
• Similar to desmosomes but totally 
different molecular structure
• Hemidesmosomes have a dense plaque 
on the cytoplasmic surface that anchors 
of  intermediate filaments.
• Integrin and type XVII collagen attach to 
the basal lamina. 
GAP JUNCTION
• Junctions that provide direct connections 
(door) between cells
• Channels or pores through the membranes 
of two cells and across the intercellular 
space
• Integrate the metabolism of the cells
• A ring of 6 membrane proteins called 
connexins - connexons
• Two connexons on neighboring membranes 
form a transmembrane channel that 
interconnects the cytoplasms of two cells
